title: First-vertex functor from opposite simplex chains preserves cocone spaces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams and right-pinched Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with universes enlarged as necessary. Let $C$ be any small ordinary category. For any small simplicial set $X$, let $\mathsf S(X)$ be the ordinary category whose objects are all simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$, including degenerate simplices, and whose morphisms $\sigma\to\tau$ are monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\sigma$; composition is composition of the monotone maps. The first-vertex functor $v_C:\mathsf S(N(C))^{\mathrm{op}}\to C$ sends the simplex $(c_0\to\cdots\to c_n)$ to $c_0$. A morphism in the opposite simplex category from a chain $\tau:[m]\to C$ to a chain $\sigma:[n]\to C$, represented by $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with $\tau\alpha=\sigma$, is sent to the arrow $\tau(0)\to\tau(\alpha(0))=\sigma(0)$. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, every map $p:N(C)\to\mathcal E$ and every vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(C),\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_{N(C)}T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(\mathsf S(N(C))^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal E)}(pN(v_C),\Delta_{N(\mathsf S(N(C))^{\mathrm{op}})}T).$$
No colimit-existence assumption on $\mathcal E$ is made, and $C$ may be empty.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, step (2), printed p. 255; Proposition 4.1.1.7, printed p. 226, with the natural join/cocone comparison for the mapping-space formulation. Online primary source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag is asserted.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathsf S(N(C))^{\mathrm{op}}$. The first-vertex rule in the statement is functorial: if $\tau\alpha=\sigma$ and $\sigma\beta=\rho$, the two assigned arrows compose to $\tau(0\to\alpha(0))$ followed by $\tau(\alpha(0)\to\alpha\beta(0))$, hence to $\tau(0\to\alpha\beta(0))$; identities give identity arrows. All these categories are small, since their objects and arrows form countable unions of sets of finite strings in $C$. Their nerves are quasicategories directly from the nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: a $2$-dimensional inner horn specifies two composable arrows, whose composite supplies its missing side; a $3$-dimensional inner horn fills by associativity; in higher dimensions all triangles are already specified, so the chain of consecutive arrows supplies the unique compatible filler. For an ordinary functor $F:B\to B'$, consider an inner-horn lifting square for $N(F)$. Fill the top horn by the unique chain in $B$ just described. Its image under $F$ and the specified bottom simplex in $N(B')$ restrict to the same inner horn; uniqueness of the ordinary-nerve filler makes these two simplices equal. This is the required lift, proving directly that $N(F)$ is an inner fibration. If $C=\varnothing$, then $A=\varnothing$ and $N(v_C)$ is the unique isomorphism between empty simplicial sets. Restriction is then the identity, proving that case. Otherwise fix $c\in C$ for the next steps.

proof.text: Define the ordinary comma category $D_c=(c\downarrow v_C)$ explicitly. Its objects are pairs $(\tau,a)$ with $\tau:[m]\to C$ and $a:c\to\tau(0)$. An arrow $(\tau,a)\to(\sigma,b)$ is a monotone map $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ satisfying $\tau\alpha=\sigma$ and $b=\tau(0\to\alpha(0))a$. Identity and composition follow from the equality in step 1. This category is also the opposite of $\mathsf S(N(c/C))$: the pair defines the chain $a:c\to\tau(0),\ \tau(0\to1)a:c\to\tau(1),\ldots$ in $c/C$, and every chain in $c/C$ is uniquely of this form. Its simplex-category arrow condition is exactly the displayed formula for $b$, with the opposite orientation. This explicitly identifies the comma category used in the source, including chains of length zero and degenerate chains.

source.place: Variant 4.2.3.15(2), printed p. 255; agent expansion of the contractible-comma argument for an arbitrary small ordinary category C; Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.7 for the final restriction assertion.

proof.text: Let $e_c$ be the object of $D_c$ consisting of the zero-simplex $c$ and $\mathrm{id}_c$. Define $H_c:D_c\to D_c$ by prepending $c$: it sends $(\tau,a)$ to the chain $(c\xrightarrow{a}\tau(0)\to\cdots\to\tau(m))$ equipped with $\mathrm{id}_c$ into its first vertex. On an arrow represented by $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, use $\alpha^+:[n+1]\to[m+1]$, where $\alpha^+(0)=0$ and $\alpha^+(i+1)=\alpha(i)+1$. The comma equality $b=\tau(0\to\alpha(0))a$ is precisely what makes the two extended chains agree after restriction by $\alpha^+$. The identities $(\alpha\beta)^+=\alpha^+\beta^+$ and $(\mathrm{id})^+=\mathrm{id}$ prove functoriality. The tail inclusion $j_m:[m]\to[m+1]$, $j_m(i)=i+1$, gives $H_c(\tau,a)\to(\tau,a)$ in $D_c$; the inclusion $k_m:[0]\to[m+1]$, $k_m(0)=0$, gives $H_c(\tau,a)\to e_c$. Their comma equalities are respectively $a=a\mathrm{id}_c$ and $\mathrm{id}_c=\mathrm{id}_c\mathrm{id}_c$. The ordinal identities $\alpha^+j_n=j_m\alpha$ and $\alpha^+k_n=k_m$ verify naturality. Thus there are natural transformations $\mathrm{id}_{D_c}\leftarrow H_c\to\mathrm{const}_{e_c}$. These are actual transformations; their components need not be isomorphisms.

source.place: Variant 4.2.3.15(2), printed p. 255; agent expansion of the contractible-comma argument for an arbitrary small ordinary category C; Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.7 for the final restriction assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] to the projection $P:D_c\to\mathbf 1$ and the section $Q:\mathbf 1\to D_c$ at $e_c$. The zigzag in step 3 connects $QP=\mathrm{const}_{e_c}$ to $\mathrm{id}_{D_c}$, and $PQ=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf 1}$. Consequently $NP:N(D_c)\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, so $N(D_c)$ is weakly contractible. This also gives contractibility in the edge-inversion formulation of the comma criterion: apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] to $NP$ and the Kan complex $\Delta^0$. For every target quasicategory it identifies functors from the point with precisely the functors from $N(D_c)$ which invert all edges, including their whole mapping spaces. Thus the point is the space obtained by inverting all arrows of this comma category.

source.place: Variant 4.2.3.15(2), printed p. 255; agent expansion of the contractible-comma argument for an arbitrary small ordinary category C; Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.7 for the final restriction assertion.

proof.text: The strict simplicial pullback $N(A)\times_{N(C)}N(c/C)$ is exactly $N(D_c)$: in each degree, a chain in $A$ and a chain in $c/C$ over the same chain in $C$ give its comma arrows and all their commuting triangles, and restriction of chains agrees on both sides. Moreover $N(c/C)$ is the coherent join undercategory $N(C)_{c/}$: its $r$-simplices are exactly strings $c\to d_0\to\cdots\to d_r$, the same as maps $\Delta^0\star\Delta^r\to N(C)$ fixing $c$. To identify the strict pullback with the categorical pullback in [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion], verify the isofibration hypothesis of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. Its projection $q:N(c/C)\to N(C)$ is an inner fibration by the chain-filler calculation in step 1. An equivalence edge in an ordinary nerve is exactly an isomorphism, since its two inverse triangles are the two ordinary inverse equations. Given $a:c\to d$ and an isomorphism $h:d\to d'$, the arrow $h:(d,a)\to(d',ha)$ is an isomorphism in $c/C$ lifting $h$ with the prescribed source; its inverse is $h^{-1}$. Thus $q$ is an isofibration in the precise sense of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Both its source and target and $N(A)$ are small quasicategories. The pullback-limit theorem now says that this strict pullback computes $N(A)\times^h_{N(C)}N(C)_{c/}$. By step 4 it is weakly contractible for every $c$.

source.place: Variant 4.2.3.15(2), printed p. 255; agent expansion of the contractible-comma argument for an arbitrary small ordinary category C; Theorem 4.1.3.1 and Proposition 4.1.1.7 for the final restriction assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] with $I=N(A)$, $J=N(C)$, $u=N(v_C)$ and $H=p$. Steps 1 and 5 establish its small-quasicategory and contractible-comma hypotheses; enlarge the containing universe to include $\mathcal E$ and its diagram categories, as the statement permits. That theorem asserts that restriction itself, for every $p$ and the specified vertex $T$, is the equivalence between the two displayed cocone mapping spaces. Its conclusion uses the same right-pinched convention, so no choice of an inverse or replacement of the restriction map is needed. Finally [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that both functor simplicial sets are quasicategories and their mapping spaces are Kan complexes. This proves the asserted equivalence of Kan complexes for every $\mathcal E,p,T$. The cited comma theorem expressly requires no colimits in $\mathcal E$, so none have been introduced.
